message.content: Pandas belong to the order Carnivora, but they are unique among carnivores because they have evolved a diet that is almost entirely herbivorous. Their evolutionary history can be traced back to the Miocene epoch (about 20–30 million years ago) when their ancestors were small, omnivorous mammals that lived in forested environments. Over time, they adapted to a specialized bamboo diet, which led to changes in their digestive system and skull morphology. The giant panda (Ailuropoda melanoleuca) is the only living member of its genus, while the extinct red panda (Ailurus fulgens) is a separate lineage that diverged from other carnivores earlier. The giant panda's closest living relatives are the bears (family Ursidae), but they split from the bear lineage around 15–20 million years ago.
